newsitem.title: UK: Kleinwort ups cash in equity portfolio, slashes U.S.
newsitem.headline: Kleinwort ups cash in equity portfolio, slashes U.S.

text.p: Kleinwort Benson has raised cash to the maximum permissible level in its model equity portfolio and slashed U.S. equities to 22 percent of its portfolio compared with 42.8 percent in the benchmark FTA World Index.

"The risks of a global equity bear market have increased sharply. We would advise clients to take extreme care over the next few months in equities," strategist Albert Edwards said in his global strategy weekly which was released on Friday.
He is most bearish on the U.S.
"The (U.S.) equity market has now discounted rapid earnings (growth), yet on a prospective basis it is still expensive relative to bonds," Edwards said.
Kleinwort prefers both bonds and cash to equities and cash is now 15 percent of its model equity portfolio.
The dollar retracement intiated by comments from Japan's Ministry of Finance will also accelerate.

"With a cap now being put on the dollar, the risk for Japanese investors incurring currency losses on the U.S. Treasuries bought over the last six months will catalyse a withdrawal from dollars, reinforcing the dollar downturn we see," Kleinwort said.
He also believes that continental European and to a lesser exent Japanese equities are vulnerable to a dollar reversal.

Edwards is overweight British, 15 percent of Kleinwort's model equity portfolio against 8.8 percent in the FTAWI, Latin America at 2.5 percent versus 0.8 percent and Japan at 33 percent versus 23 percent. -- David Chance London newsroom 44 171 542 5887
